tagline: An AI assistant that can actually run the commands — on the desktop and its own public page.
description:
mvmAI is a chat assistant wired to your own provider — Gemini, OpenAI, Groq, OpenRouter, DeepSeek, Qwen, Mistral, a local Ollama, or any OpenAI-compatible endpoint you point it at — or to a CLI tool already installed on the server, such as Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex CLI or Ollama. You bring the API key or the CLI; nothing is proxied through anyone else.

What separates it from a chat window in a browser tab is that it is on the machine. Ask it why a service will not start and it can run the commands to find out, read the output and carry on from there. Command execution stays off until an administrator turns it on, and once on, every command either waits for confirmation or runs automatically, whichever the administrator picked. When an administrator chose automatic execution and talks to Claude Code, Gemini CLI or Codex CLI, the CLI works with all of its own tools and full access to the server, like a coding assistant in a terminal, and can spend many minutes on one task; everyone else stays limited. Commands it judges dangerous are marked, and the really destructive ones are blocked entirely.

The same assistant can also be given its own public page, for visitors who are not on the desktop at all, with its own separate switch for whether those visitors may have it run commands too — off by default, and never on by accident.

Conversations are kept, renameable and deletable, and the system prompt is yours to rewrite. Images, PDF and text files can be attached to a message, administrators can attach any file or archive, and the assistant can hand a file back as a download.

With a subscription, a user can point a chat at one of their apps — add a budget transaction, plan a calendar event and more — for that user only, on the desktop and on the public page. Every change is shown as a form to check, correct and save first.

Stop ends a running reply and its CLI process. Messages typed during a reply wait in a visible queue, where you can remove them or send them into the next tool step. The assistant answers and writes into apps in your interface language unless you ask otherwise. Multiple independent app changes are reviewed as pages of one form, where each can be corrected or excluded before saving the selected changes together.
capabilities: Chat with any OpenAI-compatible provider: Gemini, OpenAI, Groq, OpenRouter, DeepSeek, Qwen, Mistral, Ollama or a custom base URL, or with a local CLI tool such as Claude Code, Gemini CLI, Codex CLI or Ollama.
CLI provider logins are installation-wide and remain tied to the Linux account that owns their credentials, even when another account opens mvmOS.

CLI assistants use mvmAI's policy-gated command transport, except for an administrator with automatic execution, whose Claude Code, Gemini CLI or Codex CLI works with all of its own tools and full access to the server.
The assistant can run shell commands on the server and read their output, once an administrator turns command execution on.
Two ways to run commands once enabled: ask for confirmation on each one, or let them run automatically.
Dangerous commands flagged, and destructive ones (rm -rf, dd, shutdown…) blocked entirely.
Approve or skip each proposed command, with the command and its reason shown first.
Optional public page so visitors can chat with the same assistant outside the desktop, with its own separate provider and command-execution controls when Premium is active.
Attach images, PDF and text files to a message; administrators can attach any file or archive, and the assistant can offer a file in its reply as a download button.

Saved conversations you can rename and delete. With Claude Code, Gemini CLI or Codex CLI each chat continues its own CLI session and sends only the new messages, and its provider and model stay fixed for the whole chat, shown to administrators with every answer.
Editable system prompt and model override.
Long tasks keep running past proxy time limits, so a CLI with full access can work for up to 30 minutes on one request.

Long conversations are compacted automatically once they pass twice the configured recent-message count, folding older messages into a running summary so per-message cost stays bounded instead of growing forever. The free plan keeps the most recent 20 messages in full; a subscription lets the administrator choose from 4 to 200.
Admins can group chats into Projects: a name, optional shared instructions (typed text and/or a file already on the server, such as CLAUDE.md), and an optional working folder.
A project with a folder shows a live file tree with git status right in the sidebar, and scopes the assistant's shell commands — and any CLI tool's own file edits — to that folder automatically.
If Git Manager is installed, a project's branch line opens that repository there directly, already selected and fetched.
Your API key stays on your server.
Premium: choose one of your apps for a chat; only that app's functions are offered, and every change is reviewed in a form before it is saved.
Stop a running reply, queue follow-up messages or send a waiting message into the next tool step.
Replies and app entries follow your interface language.
Attached pictures show as small previews before sending and in the chat, and a click enlarges them; in an older chat the administrator's images are shown again for a week.

With Premium on the desktop, a terminal can sit next to the chat: it opens over the chat or docked on the right or at the bottom, starts the command-line tool of the chat's provider in the chat's project folder, keeps its session while hidden, and can be pinned open for chosen chats.
requirements: An API key for one of the supported providers, or a local Ollama install, or another supported CLI tool already installed on the server.

integrations.name: Any app
integrations.summary: mvmAI exposes its chat endpoint to other apps on the same desktop, so they can send a prompt and get an answer using your configured provider without asking you for a second API key. RSS Reader uses this for its AI buttons.
